title: Principal faces, trivial basic-open covers, and localization restrictions
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid, written additively, and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P$ with basic opens $D(a)$ and localizations $P_a=P-\mathbf N a\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. For $a\in P$ set
$$F_a=\{c\in P:\exists d\in P,\ n\in\mathbf N,\ c+d=na\},\qquad \mathfrak m_a=P\setminus F_a.$$
Then $F_a$ is a face: it contains $0,a$, is closed under addition, and $c+e\in F_a$ implies $c,e\in F_a$. The set $\mathfrak m_a$ is a proper prime ideal in $D(a)$, and every $\mathfrak q\in D(a)$ satisfies $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m_a$. Every open neighborhood of $\mathfrak m_a$ contains $D(a)$. In particular every open cover of $D(a)$ contains $D(a)$ itself as a member. For $a=0$ one has $F_0=P^\times$ and $D(0)=X$.
For $a,c\in P$ one has
$$D(c)\subseteq D(a)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a\in F_c\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists d\in P,\ n\in\mathbf N,\ a+d=nc.$$
Under these equivalent conditions the identity of $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ induces the localization homomorphism $P_a\to P_c$, carrying $p-ma$ to the same group-completion element. It sends units to units, and its map on sharpenings sends $\operatorname{cl}_{P_a}(p-ma)$ to $\operatorname{cl}_{P_c}(p-ma)$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2--3.1.4(i),(iii), printed p.98: principal-face calculation, trivial covers, and localization transition maps; old proof steps 1--2 and the algebra in step 7.

proof.text: For $F_a$, the witnesses $(d,n)=(0,0)$ and $(0,1)$ give $0,a\in F_a$. If $x+d=na$ and $y+e=ma$, then $(x+y)+(d+e)=(n+m)a$. If $(x+y)+d=na$, then $x+(y+d)=na$ and $y+(x+d)=na$. These identities give exactly closure under addition and the face condition.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2--3.1.3, p.98: explicit additive principal-face calculation

proof.text: The complement $\mathfrak m_a$ is an ideal: if $x\notin F_a$ and $p\in P$, then $x+p\notin F_a$ by the face condition. It is proper since $0\in F_a$, and prime since its complement is closed under addition. Since $a\in F_a$, it belongs to $D(a)$. For any $\mathfrak q\in D(a)$, its complement contains $0,a$ and is closed under addition, hence contains every $na$. If $x\in F_a$ and $x\in\mathfrak q$, a witness $x+d=na$ contradicts the ideal property. Thus $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m_a$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.3--3.1.4(i),(iii), p.98: greatest prime of a basic open

proof.text: Every generated open is downward closed for inclusion of prime ideals: this holds for D(b), since b outside a larger ideal is outside a smaller one, and is preserved by intersections and arbitrary unions. Formal induction on GenerateOpen proves the assertion for the specified generated topology, without a separate basis theorem. Apply it to q contained in m_a for q in D(a) to see that every open neighborhood of m_a contains D(a). If a set S of opens contained in D(a) has supremum D(a), membership of m_a in this supremum supplies U in S containing m_a. The neighborhood result and U contained in D(a) give U = D(a), so D(a) is in S.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.4(iii), p.98: triviality of open covers

proof.text: For $a=0$, the condition $x+d=n0=0$ says exactly that $x$ is a unit, so $F_0=P^\times$. No proper ideal contains $0$, because $0+P=P$; therefore $D(0)=X$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.4(i), p.98: identity and unit cases

proof.text: If $D(c)\subseteq D(a)$, apply this to $\mathfrak m_c\in D(c)$: then $a\notin\mathfrak m_c$, so $a\in F_c$. Conversely, if $a+d=nc$ and $\mathfrak q\in D(c)$ contained $a$, the ideal property would put $nc\in\mathfrak q$, whereas $c\notin\mathfrak q$ and the complement is closed under addition and contains $0$. Thus $\mathfrak q\in D(a)$. The equivalence with existence of $d,n$ is the displayed definition of $F_c$.

Given $a+d=nc$, in $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ one has $-a=d-nc$ and hence $p-ma=(p+md)-(mn)c\in P_c$ for every $p\in P$, $m\in\mathbf N$. Thus $P_a\subseteq P_c$. Restricting the group identity gives the asserted homomorphism, independent of fraction representatives since both monoids are subsets of the same group. It fixes $P$ and sends $-a$ to the inverse of $a$, so it is precisely the localization homomorphism (these elements generate $P_a$).

If $u+v=0$ in $P_a$, their images in $P_c$ still sum to $0$; thus units map to units. If $x,y\in P_a$ differ by a unit, their images differ by its unit image. The map therefore descends to the quotient by units that defines sharpening, and on each representative it sends $\operatorname{cl}_{P_a}(p-ma)$ to $\operatorname{cl}_{P_c}(p-ma)$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.3 and Remark 3.1.4(iii), p.98: sharpening of restrictions

proof_origin.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.4(i),(iii), printed p.98; additive details of the principal-face and restriction calculations written out. Stage-3 Lean proof by B9 follows all seven calculations; the neighborhood step uses induction on the generated topology instead of a separate basis result.

lean.statement: theorem monoid_principalOpen_face (P : Type u) [CommMonoid P] (hP : IsFine P) : (∀ a : P, 1 ∈ principalFace a ∧ a ∈ principalFace a ∧ (∀ x y : P, x ∈ principalFace a → y ∈ principalFace a → x * y ∈ principalFace a) ∧ (∀ x y : P, x * y ∈ principalFace a → x ∈ principalFace a ∧ y ∈ principalFace a) ∧ (∃ m : MonoidPrime P, m.carrier = (principalFace a)ᶜ ∧ m ∈ basicOpen a ∧ (∀ q : MonoidPrime P, q ∈ basicOpen a → q.carrier ⊆ m.carrier) ∧ (∀ U : Opens (MonoidPrime P), m ∈ U → basicOpen a ≤ U)) ∧ (∀ S : Set (Opens (MonoidPrime P)), (∀ U ∈ S, U ≤ basicOpen a) → sSup S = basicOpen a → basicOpen a ∈ S)) ∧ principalFace (1 : P) = {p : P | IsUnit p} ∧ basicOpen (1 : P) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ a c : P, ((basicOpen c ≤ basicOpen a) ↔ a ∈ principalFace c) ∧ ((a ∈ principalFace c) ↔ ∃ (d : P) (n : ℕ), a * d = c ^ n) ∧ (basicOpen c ≤ basicOpen a → ∃ h : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers a) ≤ Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers c), (∀ q : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers a), IsUnit q → IsUnit (Submonoid.inclusion h q)) ∧ (∀ (q : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers a)) (r : Algebra.faceLocalization P (Submonoid.powers c)), r.val = q.val → sharpenMap (Submonoid.inclusion h) (Associates.mk q) = Associates.mk r)))
